faq.title: Common Questions
faq.description: These are the questions that come up most often in early conversations.

selection.question: What solution directions does the ZeroAnt solutions page cover?
selection.answer: The page currently focuses on three directions: life science and sterile automation, smart manufacturing with logistics collaboration, and embodied R&D with teleoperation validation. Each direction maps to a recommended combination, related applications, and a next conversation step.

precision.question: What kinds of projects fit the life science and sterile automation direction?
precision.answer: Projects focused on sample handling, liquid preparation, sterile workflows, or lab automation usually start by evaluating arms, controller hardware, vision modules, and high-precision end effectors together.

mobile.question: How is a smart manufacturing and logistics solution usually assembled?
mobile.answer: These solutions usually combine R / M / MR products with ZA-ZG100 controller hardware, navigation, and station-level interface design. They fit in-factory logistics, cross-station transfer, and mobile manipulation workflows.

delivery.question: How does ZeroAnt usually move a solution into delivery?
delivery.answer: The usual path is to confirm the task target, space limits, payload, and takt first, then combine the body, controller, and expansion modules, and finally move into pre-validation and rollout. That exposes interface boundaries earlier and reduces on-site iteration.

navigation.question: What navigation methods do your mobile robots support?

development.question: Does the robot control system support secondary development and system integration?
development.answer: Yes. We provide open SDK and API for customers to facilitate secondary development and integration with third-party systems, helping to achieve personalized function expansion.

customization.question: Can robots or systems be customized according to customer requirements?

zamr3t.summary: An embodied operation platform integrating a mobile base, lift axis, dual arms, and vision cameras for cross-area, multi-station grasping, transfer, and assembly validation.
specs: Integrated mobile base, lift axis, dual arms, and vision cameras

embodiedPlatforms.title: Embodied & Dev Platforms
embodiedPlatforms.intro: Platforms for VR, master-slave teleoperation, and embodied AI development workflows.

zarmvr.title: ZA-RMVR
zarmvr.summary: A teleoperation development platform that integrates a lift axis, dual robotic arms, dexterous hands, a controller, and VR devices for teaching, research, and embodied data collection.
specs: 1× Gigabit Ethernet + 1× USB3.0 + 10 in / 10 out I/O

zarmps.title: ZA-RMPS
zarmps.summary: A teleoperation development platform for dual-arm master-slave control, contact-task validation, and embodied data collection.
specs: Master/slave arms with 7 DOF / 640mm working radius
1× Gigabit Ethernet + 1× USB3.0 + 10 in / 10 out I/O

zardp.title: ZA-RDP
zardp.summary: A drawing and trajectory-teaching platform built on a 6-axis robotic arm for teaching demos, algorithm validation, and motion-planning experiments.

controller.title: Controller
controller.intro: Integrated control hardware for real-time motion, bus synchronization, and interface expansion.

zazg100.title: ZA-ZG100
zazg100.summary: An integrated control unit based on RK3588 for robot motion control, AI vision processing, and interface integration.
specs: EtherCAT bus, 1ms control cycle, 5μs control jitter

accessories.title: Accessories
accessories.intro: Accessories are shown in a separate section to extend travel and rotation, and can be matched after the robot body is confirmed.

rail.title: Rail Platform
rail.summary: A rail platform that extends a robot's linear working range for cross-station linkage and long-travel transfer tasks.

rotatingplatform.title: Rotating Platform
rotatingplatform.summary: A rotating platform that adds station indexing and posture adjustment for multi-angle pick-and-place and direction-change tasks.
